page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the n4 family. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, and the processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance at 1564.68 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1868.0, both falling into the average category. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression at 28.32 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 12.0 GB/sec also perform at average levels. However, multi-core and memory-intensive workloads show limitations. The Geekbench multi-core score of 4154.0, stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 3219.87, and Passmark CPU score of 5956.49 are positioned in the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only large block at 33.17 GB/sec and write large block at 21.19 GB/sec, also rank in the lower performance tier.

The n4-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing or high memory bandwidth. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-threaded and memory throughput performance relative to the allocated RAM capacity. It supports advanced CPU instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for specialized workloads. This instance is suited for moderate database operations, text processing, static web serving, and lightweight memory-intensive applications that do not saturate multi-core CPU resources.
